item.title: American schools weren’t broken until Silicon Valley used a lie to convince them they were—now reading and math scores are plummeting
item.description: Neuroscientist Jared Cooney Horvath warns that the U.S.’s $30 billion bet on laptops in schools has made Gen Zers less cognitively capable than their parents.

item.title: A dire electrician shortage is a ‘life or death’ threat to the AI data center boom—and an opportunity for Gen Z
item.description: By going all in on AI, tech companies like Meta and Microsoft are shaking up white-collar career paths—and creating a huge demand for new electricians.

item.title: CEO of America’s largest Social Security advisory firm: Trump’s big tax cut ‘did not help’
item.description: “Very few at the very top gain more and more tax advantages…the lower and middle class aren’t really seeing a benefit,” Martha Shedden told Fortune.

item.title: OpenAI’s Pentagon deal raises new questions about AI and mass surveillance
item.description: Legal experts say it is unclear if OpenAI’s contract actually provides for the restrictions on surveillance and autonomous weapons that the company says it does.

item.title: Energy markets offer ‘relatively small reaction’ to Iran war, but prices could spike if oil and gas aren’t flowing by the end of the week
item.description: Crude prices jumped 6% March 2, but they have risen 25% since the beginning of the year as tensions with Iran have escalated.

item.title: Trump’s strikes on Iran could cost American economy as much as $210 billion, top budget expert says
item.description: “One problem I have with cost-of-war calculations is that they really do ignore the counterfactual,” Kent Smetters of the Penn Wharton Budget Model told Fortune.

item.title: Interest on the $38.8 trillion national debt has tripled since 2020, and it already costs taxpayers more than defense and Medicaid
item.description: Here’s when Medicare falls below interest costs, according to CBO projections.

item.title: Blackstone CEO took home $1.2 billion last year after going ‘max everything’ with work—but he wouldn’t advise his children to put themselves under so much pressure
item.description: Blackstone cofounder Stephen Schwarzman says he put a lot of stress on himself as a young finance worker, and doesn’t want to see others burned out by daily “desperation” and “fear of failure.”

item.title: Is the media anti-tech—or just anti-crypto?
item.description: A new op-ed reflects a depressing trend by the press to portray technology in a poor light.

item.title: ‘Could it kill someone?’ A Seoul woman allegedly used ChatGPT to help carry out two murders in South Korean motels
item.description: After a South Korean woman allegedly used ChatGPT to plan two murders, questions arise into what guardrails are in place to stop people with homicidal or dangerous thoughts from using chatbots.
